prompt:
Image 1 is the pose and layout guide: four grey clay maquettes of this god in a 2 by 2 grid, one action in each cell, rendered from the game's battle camera. Copy from it exactly, cell by cell, the camera angle, the direction the body faces, the pose, the figure's size and its place in the cell. Do not copy its smooth clay surfaces, its simplified round shapes or the thickness of its limbs: the body, its anatomy and every detail follow Image 2.
Image 2 is the approved painted game cutout of this exact god, standing at rest, seen from the same camera in the same view. Paint the same individual, with exactly the same head, shapes, proportions, colours, materials, markings and equipment, in the same painting style and the same light, now in the actions of Image 1. It must be unmistakably the same god in all four cells.

One sheet: four painted figures of the same god, full body, one in each cell of a 2 by 2 grid, on a perfectly flat, uniform pure green (#00FF00) background, as game cutouts. Read left to right, top row first:
Top left: walking: a long striding step, the right foot far forward and planted, the left foot far behind on its toes, the body leaning forward, the arms swinging, the orb staff carried in its right hand.
Top right: the next step: the left foot far forward and planted, the right foot far behind on its toes, the body leaning forward, the arms swinging the other way, the orb staff carried in its right hand.
Bottom left: winding up a blow: the orb staff raised high over its right shoulder in its right hand, the body twisted back to the right and leaning back, the weight on the back foot.
Bottom right: striking: the orb staff swung round in a heavy blow in its right hand, at the moment of impact: the orb staff out level in front of the body and to its left, the body twisted round and lunging into the blow, the left foot stepped far forward.
Every cell takes its pose from Image 1, never from Image 2: Image 2 shows only what the god looks like, and its standing pose must not be copied into any cell. Each pose is strong and unmistakable at a glance. The two walking cells show a long, clearly visible stride, the legs far apart, different from each other and from the standing pose.

Camera: high above and behind, looking down at about 40 degrees, the way a player looks down at a miniature on a table; orthographic, with no perspective. The god faces away from us, toward the upper right of the image, as in Image 1 and Image 2: we see its back, its right side and the top of its head from behind; its face is hidden. It is foreshortened as seen from above: the top of the head, the shoulders or back and the upper body are large, the legs short.

Light: outdoor daylight, exactly as in Image 2; the figure stays as dark and as muted as in Image 2, lit only by small warm and cool highlights, never washed out or brightened. A high sun in the upper left of the image lights the top and the upper-left side with warm highlights; a cool blue-grey sky fill lies in the shadows on the lower-right side. No candlelight, no dramatic dark shadows. Nothing glows more than it does in Image 2. No cast shadow on the background.

Painting style: painterly oil on a wood panel, visible directional brushwork, moderate detail, exactly the hand of Image 2; a muted earthy palette with its own colours exactly as Image 2 shows them; soft painterly edges, small crisp highlights and a thin bright rim of light along the upper-left edges. A strong, simple, readable silhouette in every pose. It is not a cartoon: no cel shading, no thick black outlines, no chibi or big-headed proportions, no glossy 3D render, no pixel art.

The god: the Oracle of the Flux, a god who sees the shifting currents of magic: a tall, slender, robed seer-god, larger than a man, floating a hand's breadth above the ground. Colours: muted and earthy. The one clear colour of the figure is its robe and cowl: dull ember-orange cloth (#C4532C), the Cinder Horde's colour. All metal is dull old gold (#C9A23E), darkened and worn. Nothing in the image glows: the orb is dark smoky glass and the glyphs are thread. No other saturated area larger than a small clasp or trim.
Headgear: a deep cowl of the robe's cloth drawn forward so that it shadows the face; the lower face shows: ash-grey skin (#8F8C88), a thin calm mouth, a narrow chin; the eyes are lost in the cowl's shadow. Body: a long, flowing robe of dull ember-orange cloth (#C4532C), the Cinder Horde's colour that covers the body from the shoulders to below the feet, with no mantle and no cape; runic glyphs embroidered in lichen grey-green (#909080) thread in a band down the front and around the hem; slender ash-grey hands. The floating hem: the robe does not touch the ground; its hem drifts and frays into soft, ragged trailing wisps of cloth a hand above the ground, and no feet show. Staff: a tall straight staff of dark wood whose head is a cage of dull old gold (#C9A23E), darkened and worn bands holding a smoky dark glass orb. Proportions: tall and heroic, a towering figure with long legs (the legs about half of its height) and the head about one eighth of its height; never squat, stocky, short-legged or dwarf-like.
The orb is dark smoky glass and does not glow.

Size: in each cell the figure fills the cell exactly as its maquette does in Image 1 and stands in the same place, with clean background all round it; nothing is cropped and no part of one figure reaches into a neighbouring cell.

Background: one flat pure green (#00FF00) colour fills the whole image with no gradient, texture, floor, vignette or shadow. No green anywhere on the figure: no green cloth, no green glow, no green reflections.

Never: text, letters, numbers, labels, grid lines, dividing lines between the cells, borders, frames, signatures, logos; a floor, ground, scenery or cast shadows; blood; other creatures or people; a cropped figure; fire, flames, breath, smoke, sparks, floating embers, magic light or mist (the game draws every effect).
